newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs slip but investor buying provides support.
newsitem.headline: JGBs slip but investor buying provides support.

text.p: The benchmark September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract slipped in early Tokyo trade on Wednesday following overnight sales in London and a rise in Nikkei stocks, but the downside was holding for now on investor bargain-hunting, traders said.
The September briefly slipped as low as 124.56 just after the opening following its fall to 124.58 overnight, but had recovered to 124.60 by 0037 GMT after investor bids kicked in.
"Successive failed tries to break above 125 have confirmed topside heaviness, leaving the contract vulnerable to sales," one trust bank trader said.
The Nikkei 225 stock index, led by technology and bank shares, gained in early trade, rising 200.72 to 20,270.13.
But activity is expected to be limited ahead of a 0600 GMT news conference by Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita, with dealers divided on how much impact this is likely to have.
"I'd say chances are slight that he will say anything new, but in the absence of other factors the market has no choice but to closely watch this," a trader with a city bank's securities arm said.

The trust bank trader said some hedge selling could emerge ahead of the Matsushita news conference, making any rises difficult, and that investors were likely to be wary of aggressive bargain-hunting for the same reason.
The yield of the benchmark 182nd cash JGB was at 2.325 percent against Tuesday's Tokyo close of 2.315 percent.
